briefs.headline: Chelsea visit Liverpool in the Carabao Cup at 4 p.m. ET without Palmer, Wirtz a doubt
briefs.summary: Liverpool host Chelsea at Anfield on Wednesday in the Carabao Cup fourth round, 4 p.m. ET (8 p.m. GMT) on Paramount+, with Darren England refereeing, in the first meeting of two followed clubs this season. ESPN's team news lists Cole Palmer suspended after two yellow cards in Saturday's defeat at Tottenham, goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez out with a broken jaw, Reece James and Jamie Gittens out, and Joao Pedro a doubt with a muscle injury; Mike Penders is expected to start in goal. Liverpool, winners of four straight in all competitions after Sunday's win over Brighton, are without Hugo Ekitike, Giovanni Leoni, Conor Bradley and Jeremie Frimpong, with Florian Wirtz (ankle) and Dominik Szoboszlai (hamstring) listed as doubts.

briefs.headline: Wembanyama's 29 and 10 carry the Spurs past the Kings for a first home win
briefs.summary: Victor Wembanyama had 29 points, 10 rebounds and five blocks and San Antonio beat Sacramento one hundred thirty to one hundred three at the Frost Bank Center on Tuesday night, the Spurs' first home win of the season and second straight overall. San Antonio led by 10 after a quarter and by 26 at halftime; Devin Vassell had eight assists. De'Andre Hunter scored 24 for the Kings, who fell to none and four, and Domantas Sabonis had 20 points, 14 rebounds and eight assists. The Spurs have two wins and two losses and play at Utah on Wednesday at 9 p.m. ET.

briefs.headline: Pulisic set to sign a new AC Milan contract through 2031, ESPN reports
briefs.summary: Christian Pulisic, the United States captain, is set to sign a new contract with AC Milan running to 2031, sources told ESPN on Wednesday morning. The 28-year-old joined Milan from Chelsea in 2023. The USMNT has no match in the next seven days; the Nations League first leg against Haiti is Nov. 14 in Miami.

briefs.headline: Rays walk off the Brewers 4-3 in the 12th to deny a sweep and force Game 5
briefs.summary: Milwaukee was one inning from its first World Series title and lost it. Cooper Pratt's leadoff homer off Ian Seymour in the top of the 12th put the Brewers up 3-2 Tuesday night at Tropicana Field, and Shane Drohan then faced five Rays without an out: Junior Caminero reached on Joey Ortiz's throwing error, Liam Hicks and Jonny DeLuca singled, pinch-runner Cedric Mullins scoring to tie it, Chandler Simpson singled to load the bases and Ben Williamson's single to right won it. Tampa Bay out-hit Milwaukee 9-8 and the Brewers made two errors; David Hamilton's fifth-inning homer had put Milwaukee up 2-1 before 10 scoreless innings from both bullpens. Milwaukee still leads three games to one; Game 5 is Wednesday at 8 p.m. ET at the Trop, with Jacob Misiorowski starting for the Brewers.
briefs.source: MLB Stats API box score; AP via ESPN

briefs.headline: Colts trade Nelson to Seattle and Buckner to the 49ers as a rebuild begins
briefs.summary: Indianapolis dealt two cornerstones to the NFC West on Tuesday, two weeks before the Nov. 10 trade deadline. Eight-time Pro Bowl guard Quenton Nelson, 30, goes to the Seahawks for a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 fifth-rounder; Seattle waived guard Christian Haynes to make room. Three-time Pro Bowl defensive tackle DeForest Buckner, 32, returns to San Francisco, which traded him to the Colts in 2020, for a 2027 fourth-round pick. Both are in the final year of their contracts, and the Colts have lost three straight since firing their general manager. Elsewhere Tuesday, the Bengals put tight end Erick All Jr. on injured reserve with what is believed to be a torn ACL, the Giants put running back Tyrone Tracy Jr. on IR with a hamstring injury, and Green Bay's Matt LaFleur said Micah Parsons could practice next week for the first time since knee surgery.

briefs.headline: Tatum's overtime buzzer-beater lifts Boston; Knicks end Detroit's unbeaten start
briefs.summary: Jayson Tatum scored 40 points and hit a jumper at the overtime buzzer Tuesday as Boston beat Brooklyn one hundred twenty-five to one hundred twenty-four, leaving the Nets winless in four. New York got its first win of the season, one hundred eleven to ninety-seven over previously unbeaten Detroit, on 27 points and 20 rebounds from Karl-Anthony Towns. Portland stayed unbeaten at three and none, holding off the Lakers one hundred thirty-six to one hundred twenty-nine despite 41 points and nine assists from Luka Doncic, Deni Avdija scoring 23 for the Trail Blazers. Victor Wembanyama had 29 points, 10 rebounds and five blocks as San Antonio beat Sacramento one hundred thirty to one hundred three; the Kings are also none and four.

briefs.headline: Mississippi State loses QB Kamario Taylor for the season to toe surgery
briefs.summary: Kamario Taylor, the sophomore who carried Mississippi State to four straight wins to open the season, at Minnesota and South Carolina among them, needs surgery on the toe he injured against Missouri on Sept. 26 and will miss the rest of the season, the school said Tuesday; he tried to play through it against Alabama and Oklahoma and left both games early. Lincoln Riley, asked about his future at USC after a second loss left the Trojans' playoff hopes thin ahead of Ohio State on Saturday, said 'this is where I want to be' and called his relationship with athletic director Jen Cohen 'fantastic.' Iowa running back Kamari Moulton is out for the season with an upper-body injury, and Alabama dismissed defensive back Dre Kirkpatrick Jr., who faces misdemeanor charges. The first College Football Playoff rankings come out Nov. 3.

briefs.headline: Fourth-tier Fleetwood knock Arsenal out of the Carabao Cup on penalties
briefs.summary: Fleetwood Town of League Two put Arsenal out of the Carabao Cup on Tuesday, winning the shootout five kicks to three after a one-all draw in the round of 16, one of the biggest upsets in the competition's history. Aaron Loupalo-Bi put Fleetwood ahead in the 21st minute, Viktor Gyokeres equalised from close range in the 50th, and Arsenal finished with 10 men after Max Dowman was sent off for violent conduct in the 85th. Bradford City also advanced, past Peterborough United at Valley Parade. Wednesday's ties include Chelsea at Liverpool, Brighton at Manchester City, Aston Villa at Bournemouth, Crystal Palace at Fulham and Brentford at Sunderland. At Manchester United, Michael Carrick took training Tuesday and, per ESPN sources, expects to be in charge against Chelsea on Saturday; the club has made no announcement.

briefs.headline: Onosato targets back-to-back yusho as the Kyushu basho nears, 11 days out
briefs.summary: Yokozuna (grand champion) Onosato, 26, told reporters at the rikishi-kai (wrestlers' association meeting) at the Fukuoka Kokusai Center on Monday that 'the next tournament is what matters' as he goes for a second straight yusho (championship) at the Kyushu basho (tournament), which opens Nov. 8 at the same arena, 11 days out. Also at the meeting, Tamawashi, 41, ranked east maegashira 15 on the new banzuke (rankings), returns to the makuuchi (top) division for the first time in three tournaments as the oldest wrestler re-promoted to it since the Showa era. The JSA kyujo (absence) page is not yet live for Kyushu; no new withdrawals were reported Tuesday.

prime.item: Day 14. Proclamation SF-1-2026, issued Oct. 2 by Division of Marine Fisheries interim director Michael S. Loeffler, made the hand harvest of oysters from public bottom in internal coastal fishing waters effective at sunrise Thursday, Oct. 15, and says the season closes March 31, 2027, under Marine Fisheries Commission rule 15A NCAC 03K .0201 unless closed sooner by proclamation; as the Oct. 22 desk read it, the limit for unlicensed persons and harvesters taking oysters for personal consumption is one bushel per person per day, not to exceed two bushels per vessel per day, with a three-inch minimum shell length, no taking between sunset and sunrise, and the oyster sanctuaries of rule 15A NCAC 03R .0117 closed. The division's proclamations index, all seven pages read at 5:46 a.m. this morning, lists SF-1-2026 as issued Oct. 2 and effective at sunrise Oct. 15 and carries no later shellfish proclamation. NCDMF's recreational size and bag limits page, opened at 5:45 a.m., carries an oyster row reading three-inch shell length, one bushel per day not to exceed two bushels per vessel per day, with its footnote (I); the proclamation controls. The proclamation PDF itself was not re-opened today. Topsail Sound is coastal water under the Division of Marine Fisheries.

NCDMF's recreational size and bag limits page, opened this morning at 5:45 a.m. (HTTP 200, 108,142 bytes), lists red drum at an 18-inch minimum and 27-inch maximum total length and one per day, with the footnote that it is unlawful to possess red drum over 27 inches. The proclamations index, all seven pages read at 5:46 a.m., lists two proclamations newer than FF-47-2026, both issued Tuesday, Oct. 27, and effective 10 a.m. today: FF-48-2026, a commercial flounder order for internal coastal and joint fishing waters and Atlantic Ocean waters, gear and area specific, that closes the mobile gear northern management area and maintains the closure of the mobile gear southern management area, and M-25-2026, gill net restrictions in joint fishing waters that maintain the weekend gill net restrictions; neither is a recreational measure. FF-45-2026 and FF-46-2026 of Oct. 20, snapper-grouper measures on a gag and black grouper aggregate vessel limit and black sea bass pot stowage, took effect at 12:01 a.m. today, Oct. 28, and touch nothing in the sound. The index carries no 2026 recreational red drum proclamation. The reference calendar's October pattern has red drum running and its November pattern leads with them. The reference seasonal calendar, not a live report: the Fisherman's Post Topsail and Sneads Ferry October report, published Oct. 1, is 26.9 days old this morning and past the 21-day gate, and no November report has posted.

waters.reading: 93.8 cfs, 1.60 feet at 5:15 a.m., falling on discharge and on stage against 112.0 cfs and 1.70 feet in the fetcher's comparison.
waters.working: Under 100 cfs for the first time this fall: down 9.2 cfs and 0.05 feet on the day against the USGS trace's 103 cfs and 1.65 feet at 5:15 a.m. Tuesday, Tuesday's edition reading, an 11th straight falling morning with the recession still slowing, 148 Saturday, 128 Sunday, 112 Monday, 103 Tuesday and 93.8 this morning (20, 16, 9, 9), and the trace shows no rain bump: 103 at 6 a.m. Tuesday, 99.1 by 3 p.m., 97.3 at 9 p.m., 95.6 at midnight, 93.8 from 3 a.m. and flat through 5:15. The read string is the fetcher's own verdict, printed as it stands, "94 cfs - prime wading water.", the fetcher rounding 93.8 to 94; it still says prime wading water below 100, so the 100-cfs floor Tuesday's desk inferred for that band was not the fetcher's floor, and the band's true lower edge is not known to this desk. What the number means on the stream is thinner than the string: the fetcher's 112.0 cfs and 1.70 feet 24h_ago fields match the trace's 5:15 a.m. Monday points, about 48 hours old, so the 18-cfs drop they imply is two days' worth and the day's drop is 9; the falling flags are right. At 94 and clear after eleven days of recession the pocket water, plunge pools and undercut banks the file records as its structure are wadeable across at this flow and most pockets are too thin to hold a fish in daylight; the fish are in the plunge-pool tail-outs and the deepest runs, where they see the angler and the line before the fly. Caddis, stoneflies and sculpin are the forage the file records, so a 12-foot leader to 6X or 7X with a size 18 to 20 caddis pupa or pheasant tail under a small yarn indicator, or a size 16 elk-hair caddis with a size 20 dropper, fished from downstream up the seams and the tail-outs in the afternoon when the water is warmest; a size 8 to 10 weighted stonefly only in the deepest plunge pools; and the sculpin pattern, olive or black, swung under the undercut banks at first and last light. The Williams River in Pocahontas and Webster counties is on WVDNR's fall trout stocking schedule, code F in the 2026 Fishing Regulations Summary as the Oct. 22 desk read it, one stocking in each of two weeks beginning the third Monday of October, Oct. 19, and the second week, which began Monday, Oct. 26, runs out Friday; no outlet found by this desk's searches this morning confirms a 2026 delivery to the Williams, and WVDNR's fish-stocking page was not opened today. The fetcher carries no Williams water temperature, so none is printed.

waters.note: KNOWN FETCHER BUG, direction right and magnitude wrong this morning, the 39th logged instance: the fetcher's 112.0 cfs and 1.70 feet 24h_ago fields match the P3D trace this desk pulled at 5:44 a.m. at its Monday, Oct. 26, 5:15 a.m. points, about 48 hours old, not 24; the trace's 5:15 a.m. Tuesday point is 103 cfs and 1.65 feet, Tuesday's edition reading, so the day's move is down 9.2 cfs and 0.05 feet, falling either way. The fetcher's numbers and flags are printed as the fetcher's and the correction is here. The read string says prime wading water at 94 cfs; Tuesday's desk had described that band as 100 to 200 cfs, which the string disproves, and this desk does not know the band's floor. The trace was read for the comparison only. The Gauley and Summersville gauges were not pulled. No West Virginia NWS alert list was pulled by this desk.

waters.near: 14 miles above R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.reading: 24.86 feet at 5 a.m., steady against 25.01 in the fetcher's comparison.
waters.read: 24.9 ft — normal pool. Ordinary bank access.
waters.working: The fetcher reads the pool steady, down 0.15 against its 25.01 comparison point and inside its 0.25-foot band; against the USGS trace's 24.62 at 5 a.m. Tuesday, Tuesday's edition reading, the gauge is up 0.24 on the day, also inside the band by a hundredth, so the steady flag holds on the day though the day's direction is up where the fetcher's comparison implies down. The trace shows the pool lifted back through Tuesday: 24.56 at 3 a.m. Tuesday, its low, 24.58 at 6 a.m., climbing through 24.71 at noon and 24.88 at 9 p.m. to 24.91 at midnight, its overnight high, then 24.84 to 24.89 from 3 a.m. and 24.86 at 5, with Huntington below the dam within 0.03 of Tuesday's reading over the same hours; the Williams above showed no rain. The read string is the fetcher's band verdict, normal pool, ordinary bank access, and at 24.9 the gauge is 2.1 feet under the up-and-pushing line at 27 feet. A pool lifted a quarter foot overnight puts a little current back on the wing dams, and at normal pool the river fishes the structure and what current it makes: shad are the forage and skipjack are with them, so a white or pearl swimbait on a half-ounce head or a three-quarter-ounce spoon worked down the current face of each wing dam and along the riprap where the current breaks; a half-ounce blade bait or a jigging spoon on the lock wall's deep edge for the sauger after dark under a 94-percent moon; crawfish are the third forage the file records, so a crawfish-colored jig in the riprap for the smallmouth; and cut skipjack on the bottom in the barge cuts and the outside bends for the blues and flatheads after dark. The Corps' Huntington District site was not opened and no release figure is printed.
waters.note: This is the gauge above R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam, the pool side; the Byrd tailwater is not gauged by USGS and is not printed. KNOWN FETCHER BUG: the fetcher's 25.01 comparison point is the trace's Tuesday maximum and does not sit at the 5 a.m. Tuesday point, which was 24.62, and cannot be placed to a single hour by this desk; against 24.62 the pool is up 0.24 on the day, inside the 0.25-foot steady band, so the steady flag holds on the day while the sign of the fetcher's comparison is wrong. waters.read: 25.9 ft and falling — normal pool. Ordinary bank access.
waters.working: The fetcher reads the gauge falling, down 0.45 against its 26.36 comparison point, and the flag does not hold on the day: against the USGS trace's 25.94 at 5 a.m. Tuesday, Tuesday's edition reading, the gauge is down 0.03, well inside the fetcher's 0.25-foot steady band, so on the day the gauge is steady and the falling flag is a two-day artifact, the 26.36 figure sitting at about 6 a.m. Monday in the trace. The trace shows Tuesday flat and low: 25.93 at 6 a.m., 25.82 at 3 p.m., 25.76 at its Tuesday low, 25.84 at midnight, 25.93 at 3 a.m. and 25.91 at 5, with Point Pleasant above the dam up 0.24 over the same hours, the pool lifted a quarter foot and the gauge below it unchanged. The read string is the fetcher's band verdict, normal pool, ordinary bank access, and at 25.9 the gauge is 1.1 feet under the 27-foot line between that band and up and pushing, a 10th normal-pool morning. Steady low water below the dam leaves the fish on the current edges the structure makes: the forage is shad and skipjack with crawfish in the riprap, so a white swimbait or a three-quarter-ounce spoon worked down the current face of each wing dam rather than the eddy behind it; a half-ounce blade bait or a chartreuse-and-white paddletail on a half-ounce head along the riprap points in low light; a black-and-blue jig for the smallmouth and the drum in the rock; cut skipjack on the bottom in the barge cuts and the outside bends for the blues and the flatheads after dark; and the lock wall from the downstream side on a live skipjack for the hybrids when the gates are passing water.

waters.reading: Sound at Hampstead: low 4:23 AM at 0.1 ft, high 10:32 AM at 4.7 ft, low 5:23 PM at 0.5 ft, high 10:52 PM at 3.5 ft. Surf at Ocean City Beach pier: low 2:45 AM at -0.2 ft, high 9:24 AM at 6.2 ft, low 3:51 PM at 0.1 ft, high 9:42 PM at 4.3 ft. Water 64.8F at Beaufort, 60 miles up the coast, observed 5:30 a.m. Moon waning gibbous, 94% lit, 17.0 days old.
waters.read: Fish the moving water either side of high at 10:32 AM and 10:52 PM in the sound.
waters.working: Waning gibbous, two days past full: the fetcher's file carries the moon at 94 percent lit and 17.0 days old, and the spring tides are still on the water, the sound high holding at 4.7 feet and the surf high at 6.2 for a second morning. The sound at Hampstead bottomed at 0.1 feet at 4:23 a.m., a tenth under Tuesday's low, and is on its flood at press time, filling 4.6 feet to a 4.7-foot high at 10:32 a.m.; it drains 4.2 feet to a 0.5-foot low at 5:23 p.m., fills 3.0 feet to a 3.5-foot high at 10:52 p.m. and drains toward Thursday's early low, which falls outside today's table. All four sound events land inside today; nothing carries a spillover tag. The surf at Ocean City Beach pier runs ahead and is the bigger water: low 2:45 a.m. at -0.2, high 9:24 a.m. at 6.2, low 3:51 p.m. at 0.1, high 9:42 p.m. at 4.3, a 6.4-foot morning flood. Today's lags from the two tables are 68 and 70 minutes on the highs and 98 and 92 minutes on the lows; the lows again lag longest, the shallow sound draining slower than it fills, which stretches the ebb at the crew's spot past what a flat offset would give. NWS Wilmington has put the water back under two advisories: a Coastal Flood Advisory for Coastal Pender and Coastal Brunswick counties, issued 10:31 p.m. Tuesday, in effect 8 a.m. to noon today, up to one half foot of inundation above ground level in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways, low-lying roads and locations along the Intracoastal Waterway and adjacent tidal creeks named for minor coastal flooding, which lands on the 10:32 a.m. sound high; and a Small Craft Advisory for the coastal waters from Surf City to Cape Fear out 20 nautical miles, issued 2:26 a.m. today and running until midnight Thursday night, seas 4 to 6 feet, conditions hazardous to small craft. At 5:44 a.m. api.weather.gov carried no Rip Current Statement, Beach Hazards Statement or Gale Warning for Coastal Pender or the marine zones. The water at Beaufort, 60 miles up the coast, read 64.8F at 5:30 a.m., up four-tenths from Tuesday's edition reading of 64.4; the fetcher's file gives no reading at Topsail itself. What is running is the reference seasonal calendar, labeled as such and not a live report: the Fisherman's Post Topsail and Sneads Ferry October report, published Thursday, Oct. 1, at 9 a.m. ET, is 26.9 days old this morning and past the paper's 21-day gate, the feed still carried it as its newest item at 5:44 a.m., and no November report has posted. The calendar's October pattern is spot at the peak of the run, red drum, trout, bluefish, sea mullet and black drum; its November pattern, five days away, is red drum, speckled trout at their prime, bluefish, spot, sea mullet and blow toads, and a Beaufort thermometer in the mid-60s is the cool-down that pattern turns on. On today's tides and this water it is a tide problem before it is a lure problem, and with 4-to-6-foot seas back on the coastal waters the sound is the water that fishes: the flood runs to 10:32 a.m. with 4.7 feet over the grass and up the dock pilings, the flooded-high stage where the drum push into the grass and the dock flats, finger mullet and shrimp the forage the file records, so a quarter-ounce gold spoon or a paddletail on a three-sixteenths-ounce head along the flooded grass edges and down the dock lines on the top of the flood, with the advisory's half foot of extra water putting the fish farther back in the grass than the table alone says, and a live shrimp on a slip cork at the oyster bars and the bridge pilings for the black drum and sheepshead as the bars go under. The ebb from 10:32 a.m. to 5:23 p.m. is the day's working window, 6 hours 51 minutes of falling water still on a spring swing, 4.2 feet of water and the bait in it pulled out of the marsh; the red drum stage, the last of the fall, is roughly 3:15 to 5:15 p.m., in daylight, a live finger mullet on a Carolina rig or a three-inch Gulp shrimp under a popping cork fan-cast a couple of feet off the ICWW channel edge where the creek mouths drain the grass, and a cut mullet chunk on the bottom at the same edge as the water gets low. For spot, the same two-hook bottom rig with bloodworm or shrimp bits on the channel edges on the moving water either side of the 5:23 p.m. low, and off the piers either side of the 9:24 a.m. and 9:42 p.m. surf highs if the 4-to-6-foot seas leave the piers fishable. The flood from 5:23 to 10:52 p.m. covers the oyster bars and grass edges again, the same spoon and paddletail program, and dusk falls in the first third of that flood, the trout window the calendar is five days from calling prime: a Spook Jr. or a suspending twitch bait walked over the deeper grass edges and the dock lights in the last hour of light, then a live shrimp under a slip cork in the deeper holes on the first of the evening ebb after 10:52 p.m. under a 94-percent moon. Slack at 10:32 a.m., 5:23 p.m. and 10:52 p.m. is dead water, and on a spring tide the slack is short. Oysters are in their 14th day open under SF-1-2026 on the public bottom; the oyster bars the crew fishes over are the same structure, and the sanctuaries in rule 15A NCAC 03R .0117 are closed to harvest. Flounder are release only, the 44th day; FF-48-2026, issued Tuesday and effective 10 a.m. today, is a commercial gear-and-area order and changes nothing for the rod in the sound.
